title: Multi-tenant auth escalation: intermittent API-key org-scoping and token refresh failures in production
creator: Sanjay Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported 401/403 spikes and inability to refresh session tokens over the past 48 hours. Root symptoms varied by deployment mode: hosted saw broken token refresh during transient KV cache invalidation, dedicated experienced org-scoping misattribution during shard failover, and private customers reported KMS-backed key rotation collisions. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and rollout of a cross-environment patch.

Scope: affects API key validation, org-scoped token lookup logic, and refresh race handling in the serving runtime and auth proxy. Customers impacted: several enterprise customers (on Dedicated/Private) and a subset of Hosted tenants using short-lived session tokens.

Goal: diagnose root cause(s), deliver hotfix for Hosted immediately, coordinate Dedicated/Private patches and upgrade instructions, and provide postmortem and compensating controls (monitoring, alerting, canary rollout).
steps_to_reproduce: Hosted: simulate short-lived session token + concurrent refresh and request bursts (x1000 requests/min) -> observe 401 spikes in auth-proxy logs
Dedicated: trigger pod failover on GPU pool with live KV shard -> reproduce incorrect org lookup (user token mapped to wrong org) under high load
Private: perform KMS key rotation during active sessions and observe refresh failures and expired cache entries
root_cause:
Race conditions between token refresh handler and prefix-organized KV cache invalidation. A recent optimization (ENG-4789) introduced a lazy cache invalidation path that allowed a brief window where token-to-org mappings were stale, causing both false negatives (403) and, in rare code paths, stale mapping reads that bypassed org scoping checks. In Private deployments, KMS rotation surfaced a second failure mode where refresh logic retried with a rotated key before local cache reconciliation.

Secondary factor: insufficient per-tenant metrics for token refresh success/failure and missing tracing on org-scoping checks, which delayed detection and root cause correlation.
mitigation_actions: Hotfix: revert lazy invalidation path and deploy auth-proxy patch to Hosted (PR #5123) to force synchronous cache reconciliation on refresh requests
Emergency config: temporarily extend token TTL for affected Hosted tenants to reduce refresh frequency (applied 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC)
Dedicated: schedule rolling patch to runtime nodes with synchronous org-scoping check and KV reconciliation (maintenance window 2026-03-14)
Private: provide customer-facing upgrade bundle and migration steps for on-prem KMS rotation handling; include script to reconcile stale token mappings
Add alert: new Grafana alert on token_refresh_failure_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m across any org
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 11:12 UTC - PagerDuty triggered by elevated 401s across three Hosted clusters (on-call: Aisha Chen)
2026-03-10 11:45 UTC - Triage call with SRE, Runtime, and Auth teams; hypothesis: cache invalidation race (noted correlation with ENG-4789 rollout)
2026-03-10 14:00 UTC - Reproduced locally: concurrent refresh + request sequence -> token mapping stale for ~200-400ms
2026-03-11 02:10 UTC - Deployed Hosted hotfix (PR #5123) to canary (cluster-canary-3); observed 85% reduction in 401s within 20 minutes
2026-03-11 05:00 UTC - Edge rollout to remaining Hosted clusters completed; Dedicated customers still affected on older runtime versions
2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Private customer A reported residual failures tied to KMS rotation window; provided migration script and scheduled assistance call
Code review feedback from Auth team: add unit tests for concurrent refresh and explicit org-scope assertion; included in PR
Decision: backport fix to last two supported runtime branches and schedule Dedicated maintenance; do not change token semantics beyond TTL extension
resolution_summary: Hosted: hotfix deployed and rolled out to all clusters (2026-03-11). 401/403 rates returned to baseline. Dedicated: patch built and scheduled for rolling maintenance (2026-03-14). Private: patch and upgrade bundle delivered; one customer completed upgrade and validated fix; remaining customers scheduled. Added tracing and metrics for org-scoping and token refresh, and introduced a short-term alert. Backports prepared for runtime-1.20 and runtime-1.21. Postmortem in progress (Confluence link in links).
postmortem_actions: Add unit/integration tests for concurrent refresh + org-scope checks
Improve token refresh tracing (add span for KV lookup + org assertion)
Create runbook for KMS rotation during active sessions
Define canary criteria for future cache-invalidation changes
Customer communication: send formal incident report and mitigation timeline to impacted customers by 2026-03-16
customer_communications: 2026-03-10 13:00 UTC - Initial ack to impacted customers with temporary workaround (extend session TTL)
2026-03-11 07:00 UTC - Update: Hosted hotfix deployed; monitoring shows stabilization
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - Dedicated customers notified of scheduled maintenance window
2026-03-13 10:00 UTC - Private customers provided upgrade bundle and support window
